Feature.Description:
Pan/tilt movement and position presets of the camera (via ONVIF PTZ).
Coordinate system (normalized ONVIF generic space, unitless, range -1.0 to +1.0 on both axes): Origin (Pan 0, Tilt 0): the direction the camera faces after power-up, i.e. the side of the camera body with the logo. MoveHome returns to it. Pan : positive = turn to the LEFT as seen from behind the camera (counter-clockwise viewed from above, for a camera standing on a table). Negative = turn to the right. -1.0 to +1.0 spans the mechanical pan range of 340 degrees (Tapo C232), i.e. about 170 degrees per 1.0: Pan +1.0 is about 170 degrees left, -1.0 about 170 degrees right. Example: to turn about 90 degrees to the left, use MoveRelative with DeltaPan = +0.53. Tilt: positive = UP, negative = DOWN. -1.0 to +1.0 spans the mechanical tilt range of 69 degrees (Tapo C232), i.e. about 35 degrees per 1.0. Note: the product page also states "360 degrees pan / 110 degrees tilt"; those are the visible coverage including the lens field of view, not the movement range. The degree values assume a linear mapping derived from the specification and were only roughly confirmed by eye on a Tapo C232 (pan: Pan -0.5 to +0.5 looked like about 170 to 180 degrees). Treat them as approximations. For a ceiling-mounted camera the directions may be inverted (not verified). Other camera models may have different mechanical ranges.
Movement behavior (Tapo C232): The camera moves pan first, then tilt. Pan speed is about 0.19 per second (about 32 degrees per second); a full pan sweep from -1.0 to +1.0 takes about 11 seconds, plus up to about 5 seconds of tilt. Movement commands finish only when the camera has stopped, and return the final position. Only one movement can run at a time; a movement command issued while another is running is rejected with MovementInProgress. Snapshots and recordings may run during movements.
Presets: at most 8 presets can be stored in the camera (Tapo C232). Presets are identified by a token assigned by the camera and have a name chosen by the user. Preset names are unique on this server: saving with an existing name updates that preset.

Command.Description: Move to an absolute pan/tilt position and wait until the camera has stopped. See the feature description for the meaning of the coordinates.

Parameter.Description: Target pan, -1.0 (about 170 degrees right) to +1.0 (about 170 degrees left); 0 = power-up front.
Target tilt, -1.0 (lowest) to +1.0 (highest); 0 = power-up tilt. About 35 degrees per 1.0.
Pan offset, -2.0 to +2.0. Positive = left. About 170 degrees per 1.0.
Tilt offset, -2.0 to +2.0. Positive = up. About 35 degrees per 1.0.

Command.Description: Move to Pan 0, Tilt 0 (the power-up front direction) and wait until the camera has stopped.
List the presets stored in the camera.
Move to a stored preset and wait until the camera has stopped.
Store the current position as a preset with the given name. If a preset with the same name already exists, its position is updated and its token is kept.

Parameter.Description: Preset name: 1 to 32 bytes in UTF-8 (e.g. up to 32 ASCII characters or about 10 Japanese characters). The characters & < > " ' are not allowed (the camera cannot handle them).

Property.Description: Current pan/tilt position as reported by the camera (may change while moving).

DefinedExecutionError.Description: The camera could not be reached or returned an error. The message contains details.
The command cannot be executed because the status is Not Connected or Error. Use Reset first.
Another movement command is still running. Wait for it to finish and retry.
No preset with the given token exists. Use GetPresets to list valid tokens.
The camera cannot store more presets (8 on Tapo C232). Remove a preset first.
The preset name is longer than 32 bytes in UTF-8.

DataTypeDefinition.Description: Normalized pan or tilt position, -1.0 to +1.0 (see the feature description).
Normalized pan or tilt offset, -2.0 to +2.0 (see the feature description).
A pan/tilt position in normalized coordinates (see the feature description).

Element.Description: Pan, -1.0 to +1.0. Positive = left of the power-up front, about 170 degrees per 1.0.
Tilt, -1.0 to +1.0. Positive = up, about 35 degrees per 1.0.
Identifier assigned by the camera; use it with GotoPreset and RemovePreset.
